facts.label: HSC students and entry (University of Auckland)

value.text: The Bangladesh HSC is not on the University of Auckland's 2027 lists of overseas school qualifications for direct entry, so HSC students apply to its foundation programme first, or ask the university. A levels are on the list.

facts.where: Country lists in the A to I and J to Z documents, approved for Semester 1 2027 onwards
facts.note: The lists do not say in words that the HSC is refused, so ask the university. Otago, Massey, Waikato, Lincoln and AUT take the HSC directly. Note 5 of the A to I list covers Cambridge International and Edexcel A levels.

facts.label: Foundation programme (University of Auckland)

value.text: Foundation study usually takes a year, or 8 months on the accelerated programme. Completing it gives guaranteed entry with the required average and IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5. Some programmes ask for more.

facts.where: Why study a foundation programme, and the entry conditions
facts.note: UP Education, which runs the programme, gives 6 months for the accelerated version and 8 to 9 months for fast-track.

facts.label: Foundation programme lengths (University of Auckland International College)
facts.where: University of Auckland International College table: Duration row
facts.note: To start, accelerated needs IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, fast-track 5.5 with no band below 5.0, and standard 5.0 with no band below 4.5. The University of Auckland's own page describes the usual length as a year, with an accelerated 8-month version.

facts.label: The SAT route (University of Auckland)

value.text: SAT-based entry also requires a high school diploma from a regionally accredited US high school, so it is open only to students who hold one. Medicine, pharmacy, optometry and medical imaging have no direct entry from school.

facts.where: Note 3, and the notes on programmes without direct entry

facts.label: Money needed for living costs
facts.where: Section on money for living costs
facts.note: NZD 20,000 for each year the visa covers, which is normally the period of study you have paid for, usually the first year. You do not need the money for later years now, but a believable plan for paying them helps your application. If your tuition is not paid yet, the money you show must cover the tuition too. Add money for a ticket out of New Zealand, or a paid ticket. For study shorter than a year, NZD 1,667 a month.

facts.label: Student visa application fee
facts.where: Top of the page: Cost, from NZD 850
facts.note: Worked out from the fee table from 1 October 2024: a NZD 485 fee and a NZD 265 immigration levy, plus the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy. A Visa Application Centre charges its own service fee if you use one; these rose on 1 January 2026 in countries including Bangladesh.

facts.label: Chest X-ray and medical checks

value.text: A student staying more than 6 months must have a chest X-ray if they are a citizen of, or have spent more than 3 months in the last 5 years in, a country without a low incidence of tuberculosis. Full fee-paying students do not usually need a medical certificate.

facts.note: Bangladesh is not on Immigration New Zealand's low-tuberculosis list (see the next fact). X-rays are done by panel physicians approved by Immigration New Zealand, described on its page on who needs an X-ray, and must be less than 3 months old when they are received.

facts.label: Police certificate

value.text: Applicants aged 17 or older whose total time in New Zealand will be 24 months or longer must provide police certificates less than 6 months old when they apply, from each country of citizenship. A receipt showing that you have applied for one is not accepted.

facts.note: Immigration New Zealand said in July 2026 that police certificates must be sent with the application; an application without one may be declined. A certificate sent with an earlier visa application is accepted if it was issued in the last 36 months.

facts.label: Tuition before the visa

value.text: You must show that you have paid the tuition fees for 1 course, or 1 year of study, whichever is shorter, with a receipt or letter from your university. If you apply from outside New Zealand, you can wait to pay until Immigration New Zealand approves your application in principle; the visa is issued only after you send proof of payment.

facts.where: Sections on proof of tuition fees and approval in principle
facts.note: You can apply with a conditional offer of place, but you need an unconditional offer before the visa is approved. Waiting to pay makes processing take longer.

values.where: Top of the page: Processing time, 80% within 8 weeks
values.note: One in five applications takes longer.

values.where: Top of the page: Processing time, 80% within 7 weeks
values.note: One in five applications takes longer. Immigration New Zealand advises applying at least 3 months before you travel.

facts.label: When to print the bank statement (Massey University)

value.text: After paying fees, and less than 2 weeks before lodging the visa application.

facts.note: Massey University's rule, from its checklist of 22 May 2025. Immigration New Zealand lets you apply before paying tuition (see visa.tuitionFirst); this rule is for students who pay first.

facts.label: Length of a bachelor's degree in New Zealand

value.text: A bachelor's degree is a level 7 qualification that normally needs at least three years of full-time study.

facts.note: A bachelor's degree with honours can be a four-year degree, as engineering usually is.

Entry with the HSC or A levels (University of Otago)

value.text: Direct entry with the Bangladesh HSC and a GPA of at least 4.0 out of 5.0. UK A levels: three passes at grade C or higher. Cambridge International: at least 120 points on the New Zealand tariff.

facts.label: New Zealand tariff for Cambridge International (University of Otago)

value.text: A level grades count A* 140, A 120, B 100, C 80, D 60 and E 40 points; AS level grades count A 60, B 50, C 40, D 30 and E 20. Entry needs at least 120 points from at least three syllabus groups, with a D or better in three groups, not counting Thinking Skills. Literacy and numeracy rules also apply.

facts.label: Entry with the HSC (Massey University)

value.text: Direct entry with the Bangladesh HSC or Alim and a GPA of at least 4.0 out of 5.0. A levels are considered case by case. Students without the qualifications can take Massey's foundation certificate first.

facts.where: Bangladesh row and the section on foundation study

facts.label: Entry with the HSC or A levels (University of Waikato)

value.text: Direct entry with the Bangladesh HSC or Alim and a GPA of at least 4.0 out of 5.0. UK A levels: at least 6 points from three subjects, with a C in at least one. Cambridge International: at least 120 points on the New Zealand tariff.

facts.label: Entry with the HSC (Lincoln University)

value.text: Direct entry with the Bangladesh HSC and a GPA of at least 4 out of 5. Cambridge International: at least 120 points on the New Zealand tariff, with an E in an AS level English subject and a D in IGCSE maths.

facts.label: Entry with the HSC or A levels (Auckland University of Technology)

value.text: Direct entry with the Bangladesh HSC and a GPA of at least 4.0 out of 5.0. A levels: three, with at least one at grade C or better. Cambridge International: 120 points with three subjects at grade D or above.

facts.label: Entry with A levels (Victoria University of Wellington)

value.text: A levels taken outside the UK: three passes, with at least one at grade C or higher.

facts.note: Victoria's HSC rule is on a country list that could not be read, so ask Victoria about the HSC.

facts.label: Counting the tariff (Victoria University of Wellington)

value.text: Up to six subject units count, no more than two from one syllabus group, and an A level counts as two units. The best six count.

facts.where: Paragraph on how points are counted
facts.note: Victoria uses the same points for each grade as the University of Otago.

facts.label: HSC entry to the pathway programmes (UC International College)

value.text: The Certificate in Foundation Studies needs the HSC with an overall GPA of at least 4.0. The Diploma in University Studies, which counts as the first year of a University of Canterbury degree, needs an overall GPA of 4.5; for engineering you also need a grade of 5.0 in mathematics, physics and chemistry.

facts.note: The University of Canterbury's own HSC rule could not be read, so ask UC whether it takes the HSC directly.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Auckland)

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 4.0 with 4.0 in writing on the new scale (80 with 21 on the old), or PTE Academic 50 with no communicative score below 42. The Duolingo English Test is not on the list. An A level in English endorsed by a UK board, at grade E, also counts.

facts.where: Accepted tests and A level English, for Semester 1 2027 onwards

facts.label: English requirement (University of Otago)

value.text: IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 4 with 4 in writing on the new scale (80 with 20 on the old), PTE Academic 50 with no communicative skill below 42, or Duolingo 105 with no subscore below 95. An A level in English endorsed by a UK board, at grade E, also counts.

facts.note: Results must be from no more than two years before you begin your study at Otago.

facts.label: English requirement (Massey University)

value.text: IELTS 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each band, TOEFL iBT 4.0 with 4.0 in writing on the new scale (80 with 19 on the old), PTE Academic 50 with at least 42 in each skill, or Duolingo 105 with at least 95 in each band. Results are valid for 2 years.

facts.label: English requirement (Victoria University of Wellington)

value.text: IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 80, PTE Academic 50 with no communicative score below 42, or Duolingo 105 with no band below 95. An A level in English at grade E also counts.

facts.note: The page gives TOEFL only on the old scale.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Canterbury)

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each part, TOEFL iBT 4.0 on the new scale (80 with at least 19 in each part on the old), or PTE Academic 50 with no communicative skill below 42. The Duolingo English Test is not listed for degrees.

facts.note: TOEFL scores must come from a single test date. On the new scale UC also sets 3.0 in listening, writing and speaking and 3.5 in reading.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Waikato)

value.text: IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 80 with 21 in writing, PTE Academic 50 with no communicative skill below 42, or Duolingo 105 with no band below 95. PTE Academic Online is not accepted. An E in certain English-intensive A level subjects counts as IELTS 6.0.

facts.label: English requirement (Auckland University of Technology)

value.text: IELTS 6.0 with every band 5.5 or higher, TOEFL iBT 80, PTE Academic 50 with no score below 42, or Duolingo 105. The online versions of IELTS and PTE are not accepted. Studies taught and assessed mainly in English can also count, with evidence.

facts.note: Ask AUT whether your school's English-medium teaching counts. TOEFL is given on the old scale, with 15 in reading and listening, 18 in speaking and 20 in writing.

facts.label: University of Otago Global Scholarship

value.text: NZD 15,000 towards first-year tuition for new international bachelor's students with a passport from one of 13 countries, including Bangladesh. You are assessed automatically when you apply, with no separate application, and offers are unlimited.

facts.note: Selection is on academic potential, as shown by admission to your programme. Otago may change the country list. It does not cover foundation study. Otago also gives a NZD 10,000 Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship, assessed automatically.

facts.label: Undergraduate International Study Grant (Massey University)

value.text: NZD 15,000 towards tuition for one year, for new international students from any region starting a listed bachelor's degree in 2027. There is no separate application.

facts.note: Not for holders of fully funded government scholarships.

facts.label: VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship (Victoria University of Wellington)

value.text: NZD 15,000 towards first-year tuition for every new international student entering the first year of a bachelor's degree, assessed with the application.

facts.note: Not for government-sponsored students or students with credit transfer. It applies to one year only and cannot be deferred to a later year.

facts.label: UC International First Year Scholarship (University of Canterbury)

value.text: NZD 15,000 for first-year full-time undergraduates studying from overseas, with up to 7 awards.

facts.label: Vice-Chancellor's International Excellence Scholarship (University of Waikato)

value.text: Up to NZD 15,000 towards tuition for first-time international students with excellent academic results. Apply in MyWaikato after you apply to enrol.

facts.note: The page lists 30 November for Trimester A offers, but also says applications are reviewed monthly and that the closing date does not apply.

facts.label: AUT International Scholarships, South Asia (Auckland University of Technology)

value.text: NZD 10,000 towards first-year bachelor's tuition, for students from South Asia, including Bangladesh. Apply by 22 November 2026 for Semester 1 2027, or by 23 May 2027 for Semester 2.

facts.where: Regulations: value, eligibility and closing dates
facts.note: Awards are made every two weeks until places are filled, so apply early.

facts.label: Dean's Asia Scholarship, business and economics (University of Auckland)

value.text: Full international tuition fees and compulsory health insurance for up to 360 points, for up to three students from Asia, including Bangladesh, starting a Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Property. Students who have done any secondary or tertiary study in New Zealand are not eligible.

facts.where: Regulations: value, number on offer, countries covered and eligibility
facts.note: This includes a foundation programme taken in New Zealand. The scholarship page gives the current round as 10 September to 22 October 2026; expect the next round in September and October 2027.

facts.label: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships

value.text: Bangladesh is not on the list of countries eligible for Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships.

facts.label: Bangladesh and the tuberculosis list

value.text: Bangladesh is not on Immigration New Zealand's list of countries with a low incidence of tuberculosis.

facts.label: Bank statements for the student visa

value.text: Bank statements must show the account holder's name and three months of transactions. If your tuition is already paid, the evidence of money should be dated after the payment. Immigration New Zealand may ask where the money came from.

facts.note: Screenshots of bank transfers and receipts from education agents are not accepted. Deposits over NZD 2,000 must be explained with documents. Fixed deposits must have been held for at least 3 months. Your tuition fees are in addition to living costs.

facts.label: Recent student visa waits for university students

value.text: In the last 4 weeks, half of the applications for university study were decided within 2 weeks, and 80% within 5 weeks.

facts.note: Updated weekly, counted in working days.

facts.label: How to apply for the student visa

value.text: Apply online, upload your documents and pay the fees. Apply at least 3 months before you plan to travel; the busiest time is between October and March. The visa is normally issued for the period of study you have paid for, up to 4 years.

facts.note: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave New Zealand.

facts.label: Student visa interviews

value.text: Immigration New Zealand interviews some student visa applicants. It recorded 22,067 student visa interviews from 2018 to 2022. Bangladeshi applicants outside New Zealand were interviewed 44 times in 2018, 57 times in 2019 and 12 times in 2020, and none were recorded in 2021 or 2022.

facts.where: Tables of interviews by year and nationality
facts.note: From Immigration New Zealand's reply to an Official Information Act request, published on FYI.org.nz.

facts.label: Working while you study in New Zealand

value.text: Up to 25 hours a week during study, and full time in all scheduled holidays, for student visas granted from 3 November 2025.

facts.note: The limit was 20 hours before 3 November 2025. Full-time holiday work needs a course of 120 credits.

facts.label: Post Study Work Visa

value.text: Up to 3 years of open work in New Zealand, depending on the level of your qualification and how long you studied for it. A bachelor's degree must have been studied full time for at least 30 weeks in New Zealand. You need at least NZD 5,000 and must apply no later than 3 months after your student visa expires.

facts.label: Post Study Work Visa fee
Post Study Work Visa changes from 16 November 2026

value.text: From 16 November 2026, applications are made through Immigration Online, and graduates with a level 7 graduate diploma who also hold a bachelor's degree become eligible, if they studied full time in New Zealand for the whole qualification.

facts.note: Only one Post Study Work Visa can be granted to a person.

facts.label: Living costs for a student

value.text: Around NZD 20,000 to 27,000 a year in Auckland and Wellington, and NZD 18,000 to 21,000 in Dunedin, home of the University of Otago.

facts.note: The page gives no year. Food is at least NZD 80 to 120 a week, and a room in a shared house starts at NZD 140 a week.

facts.label: Visa scams

value.text: You are not required to use an adviser. Immigration New Zealand never asks you to pay visa fees into a bank account, its emails end in immigration.govt.nz or mbie.govt.nz, and New Zealand employers cannot charge you fees for a job.

facts.note: A visa can be checked with Immigration New Zealand's Visa Verification service.

facts.label: Education agents and visa advice

value.text: An education agent outside New Zealand may advise on student visas only. Advice on any other visa must come from a licensed immigration adviser.

facts.note: Licensed advisers are on the Immigration Advisers Authority's public register.

facts.label: Student visas for Bangladeshi citizens in 2025

value.text: In 2025, Immigration New Zealand approved 813 fee-paying student visa applications from Bangladeshi citizens.

facts.note: Immigration New Zealand's figures, republished by Figure.NZ; totals are randomly rounded to multiples of three.

facts.label: Insurance for the student visa

value.text: You must agree to have insurance for travel and any health care you need, from the start of your course until your visa expires. The policy must meet the Code of Practice for international learners and be acceptable to your university.

facts.note: Your university will tell you what your policy must cover, or may arrange it for you.

facts.label: Medical and travel insurance for foundation students (UP Education)

values.where: Insurance section, accurate as of 10 March 2026
values.note: Compulsory for UP Education's foundation students. Universities set their own insurance, so ask yours.

facts.label: Application period for international students (University of Otago)

value.text: The main international application period is 1 May to 15 November, for studies starting in semester 1 (February).

facts.note: All applications are made online.

facts.label: Application fee for international applicants (University of Auckland)
facts.where: Fee for applicants whose highest qualification is from an overseas secondary school
facts.note: No fee when you apply through a registered agent. NZD 100 if your highest qualification is from a university or college abroad.
